title: Rainfall as IV for agricultural loan demand

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Two-Stage Least Squares (Instrumental Variables).

Why IV?  
Loans per capita (x) may be endogenous: higher‐yield farms could self-select into borrowing more, and unobserved farm ability can drive both credit take-up and output. Annual rainfall deviation (z) is used as an instrument because:  

1. Relevance – Rainfall shocks affect farmers’ need for external finance (first-stage condition).  
2. Exclusion – Conditional on land size and soil quality, rainfall affects output only through its impact on credit, not directly (exclusion restriction).

Key assumptions  
• Instrument relevance: Cov(z, x | controls) ≠ 0.  
• Instrument exogeneity: Cov(z, u) = 0, where u is the structural error in the yield equation.  
• Monotonicity/linear first stage (standard 2SLS conditions).  

With a single cross-section and one instrument, 2SLS identifies the causal elasticity of yield with respect to credit under these assumptions.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load libraries
library(AER)       # ivreg
library(sandwich)  # robust vcov
library(lmtest)    # coeftest
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Read the data -----------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s19_data.csv",
               col_types = cols(
                 y = col_double(),
                 x = col_double(),
                 z = col_integer(),
                 controls = col_double()
               ))

# 2. Quick summary -----------------------------------------------------------
cat("Observations:", nrow(df), "\n\n")
print(summary(df))

# 3. OLS benchmark -----------------------------------------------------------
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
cat("\nOLS (robust SE):\n")
print(coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1")))

# 4. First stage -------------------------------------------------------------
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
cat("\nFirst-stage regression (robust SE):\n")
print(coeftest(first_stage, vcov = vcovHC(first_stage, type = "HC1")))
fs_fstat <- linearHypothesis(first_stage, "z = 0", vcov = vcovHC(first_stage, type = "HC1"))$F[2]
cat("Robust first-stage F-statistic on instrument z:", round(fs_fstat, 2), "\n")

# 5. 2SLS estimation ---------------------------------------------------------
iv <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
iv_se <- vcovHC(iv, type = "HC1")
cat("\n2SLS results (robust SE):\n")
print(coeftest(iv, vcov = iv_se))

# 6. Weak-instrument diagnostics --------------------------------------------
# Stock-Yogo critical values are rule-of-thumb; we compare Cragg-Donald F.
cd <- summary(iv, diagnostics = TRUE)
cat("\nCragg-Donald statistic:", round(cd$diagnostics["weak instruments", "statistic"], 2), "\n")

# 7. Robustness: add squared rainfall as control to soak direct rainfall effect
df <- df %>% mutate(z2 = z^2)
iv_robust <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls + z2 | z + z2 + controls, data = df)
iv_robust_se <- vcovHC(iv_robust, type = "HC1")
cat("\nRobustness: include z^2 as control\n")
print(coeftest(iv_robust, vcov = iv_robust_se))

# 8. Print key coefficient ---------------------------------------------------
beta_iv <- coef(iv)["x"]
se_iv   <- sqrt(diag(iv_se))["x"]
cat("\n=== KEY RESULT ===\n",
    "2SLS elasticity of yield w.r.t. credit (beta):", round(beta_iv, 3),
    " | Robust SE:", round(se_iv, 3), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Economic intuition suggests that better access to credit allows farmers to purchase improved seeds, fertilizers and machinery, raising productivity. Hence:

• First stage: positive and significant (rainfall ↑ → credit demand ↑), F-stat > 10.  
• Second stage: coefficient on credit (β) positive, roughly 0.3–0.5 – i.e., a 1 % increase in loans per capita raises crop yield by about 0.3–0.5 %. Robustness check with added z² should leave the estimate similar, supporting the exclusion restriction.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV/2SLS — instrument: rainfall; first stage: rainfall → loans; exclusion restriction: rainfall ⊥ yield | credit
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Credit access significantly increases crop yields
_ground_truth.main_effect: 10% increase in credit → 4% yield increase (IV estimate)
